heroHeadline: PLA Sorties Ease to 5/Day Post-Drill but All Cross the Median Line as Ship Presence Hits Window High of 17 on Sep 20; 20 Sorties (13 Crossing) on Sep 19; A Senior US Official Disputes Report That Beijing Threatened to Cancel the Sept 24 Trump-Xi Summit Over a Pending Taiwan Arms Sale
heroSubtitle: PLA gray-zone pressure eased in sortie volume after the Sep 16-18 Jioupeng Base live-fire drill window (which peaked at 28 sorties, 24 crossing, on Sep 18), falling to 20 sorties (13 crossing) on Sep 19 and just 5 sorties on Sep 20 — but every one of those 5 crossed the Taiwan Strait median line, and the accompanying naval and coast-guard presence kept climbing: 11 PLAN vessels plus 6 official ships (17 total) on Sep 20 is the highest ship count recorded since the Sep 7 surge, suggesting the center of gravity is shifting from aircraft sorties toward a sustained maritime presence. Separately, a senior US official close to the Trump administration disputed as inaccurate a Sep 12-13 report that Beijing had threatened to cancel President Xi Jinping's planned Sep 24 White House visit unless Washington withheld approval of a pending $14 billion Taiwan arms package, though analysts remain split on how seriously to weigh the underlying threat ahead of that summit. Earlier in the window, Premier Cho Jung-tai inaugurated the NT$1.4 billion Taiwan-Matsu No. 4 subsea cable (Sep 18) and MAC Deputy Minister Shen Yu-chung reaffirmed that Washington remains committed to first-island-chain deterrence (Sep 18), while President Lai inspected the final day of the Jioupeng drill as a Chinese reconnaissance drone shadowed the exercise off Taitung (Sep 18).
